questions.title: Count triangular work
questions.question: Given an integer n, return the number of visits performed by loops i=0..n-1 and j=0..i. Do not execute the loops in your final implementation.
constraints: 0 <= n <= 1000000; return an exact Number integer.
questions.input_output: Call solve(input) with the JSON input shape in each fixture; return a JSON-compatible result.
hints: Sum row lengths 1 through n.
questions.solution_code: function solve(n) { return n * (n + 1) / 2; }
questions.detailed_explanation: Loop counting is O(n^2); algebraic summation is constant-time under this bounded-number model. Sum row lengths 1 through n.
expected_answer_elements: Sum row lengths 1 through n.
State the invariant.
Time: O(1); auxiliary space: O(1).

questions.title: Growth-copy accounting
questions.question: A dynamic buffer starts at capacity 1 with length 0. Before each append to a full buffer, double capacity and copy its current contents. Given n appends, return total copied items, excluding the new appends.
constraints: 0 <= n <= 1000000; growth happens only when an append would exceed capacity.
questions.input_output: Call solve(input) with the JSON input shape in each fixture; return a JSON-compatible result.
hints: Account for a geometric series of capacity copies.
questions.solution_code: function solve(n) { let capacity = 1, copied = 0; while (capacity < n) { copied += capacity; capacity *= 2; } return copied; }
questions.detailed_explanation: Simulating all appends is O(n); summing growth events is O(log n). Total copying is less than 2n. Account for a geometric series of capacity copies.
expected_answer_elements: Account for a geometric series of capacity copies.
State the invariant.
Time: O(log n); auxiliary space: O(1).
Cover empty, boundary and adversarial inputs.

questions.title: Telemetry frequency table
questions.question: Given an array of lowercase event names, return [name,count] pairs sorted lexicographically by name. Treat repeated names as the same event type.
constraints: 0 <= events.length <= 100000; names contain only lowercase ASCII letters.
questions.input_output: Call solve(input) with the JSON input shape in each fixture; return a JSON-compatible result.
hints: Count with a map and sort only distinct names.
questions.solution_code: function solve(events) { const counts = new Map(); for (const name of events) counts.set(name, (counts.get(name) || 0) + 1); return [...counts].sort((a,b) => a[0] < b[0] ? -1 : a[0] > b[0] ? 1 : 0); }
questions.detailed_explanation: Repeated full-array scans are quadratic; hashing is expected linear before sorting u unique keys. Count with a map and sort only distinct names.

State the invariant.
Time: O(n + u log u); auxiliary space: O(u).

questions.title: Batched range totals
questions.question: Input is {values,queries}. Each query [left,right] uses inclusive zero-based bounds. Return each range sum in query order.
constraints: 0 <= values.length <= 100000; queries are valid nonempty ranges; integer sums remain safe integers.
questions.input_output: Call solve(input) with the JSON input shape in each fixture; return a JSON-compatible result.
hints: Store a leading-zero prefix and subtract at the two boundaries.
questions.solution_code: function solve({values,queries}) { const prefix=[0]; for (const value of values) prefix.push(prefix[prefix.length-1]+value); return queries.map(([l,r]) => prefix[r+1]-prefix[l]); }
questions.detailed_explanation: Scanning each range costs O(nq); preprocessing makes each valid query constant-time. Store a leading-zero prefix and subtract at the two boundaries.

questions.title: Unique-event window
questions.question: Given an array of event names, return the length of the longest contiguous block containing no repeated name.
constraints: 0 <= events.length <= 100000; event identity is exact string equality.
questions.input_output: Call solve(input) with the JSON input shape in each fixture; return a JSON-compatible result.
hints: Advance the left boundary past the last occurrence, never backwards.
questions.solution_code: function solve(events) { const seen=new Map(); let left=0,best=0; for(let right=0;right<events.length;right++){ if(seen.has(events[right])) left=Math.max(left,seen.get(events[right])+1); seen.set(events[right],right); best=Math.max(best,right-left+1); } return best; }
questions.detailed_explanation: Enumerating and checking every interval is superlinear; each boundary advances monotonically. Advance the left boundary past the last occurrence, never backwards.
expected_answer_elements: Advance the left boundary past the last occurrence, never backwards.
State the invariant.
Time: O(n) expected; auxiliary space: O(u).

questions.title: Signed target windows
questions.question: Input is {values,target}. Return the number of nonempty contiguous subarrays whose sum equals target; values may be negative.
constraints: 0 <= values.length <= 100000; values and counts remain safe integers.
questions.input_output: Call solve(input) with the JSON input shape in each fixture; return a JSON-compatible result.
hints: Count earlier prefixes equal to current prefix minus target.
questions.solution_code: function solve({values,target}) { const counts=new Map([[0,1]]); let prefix=0,result=0; for(const value of values){ prefix+=value; result+=counts.get(prefix-target)||0; counts.set(prefix,(counts.get(prefix)||0)+1); } return result; }

questions.title: Bounded recency cache
questions.question: Input is {capacity,operations}, where operations are ['put',key,value] or ['get',key]. Return an array containing each get result or null for a miss. A get or overwrite makes the key most recent; evict least recent on overflow.
constraints: 1 <= capacity <= 1000; keys are strings; up to 10000 operations; stored values are integers.
questions.input_output: Call solve(input) with the JSON input shape in each fixture; return a JSON-compatible result.
hints: Refresh insertion order on both get and overwrite; then remove the first key on overflow.
questions.solution_code: function solve({capacity,operations}) { const cache=new Map(),out=[]; for(const [action,key,value] of operations){ if(action==='get'){ if(!cache.has(key)){out.push(null);continue;} const saved=cache.get(key); cache.delete(key);cache.set(key,saved);out.push(saved); } else {cache.delete(key);cache.set(key,value); if(cache.size>capacity) cache.delete(cache.keys().next().value);} } return out; }
questions.detailed_explanation: The JavaScript reference uses Map order. Implement a hash map plus doubly linked nodes as the independent language-neutral variation; never claim Map provides a portable linked-list API. Refresh insertion order on both get and overwrite; then remove the first key on overflow.
expected_answer_elements: Refresh insertion order on both get and overwrite; then remove the first key on overflow.
State the invariant.
Time: O(m) expected with insertion-ordered Map; auxiliary space: O(c) auxiliary.
Cover empty, boundary and adversarial inputs.

questions.title: Validate nested brackets
questions.question: Given a string consisting only of ()[]{}, return whether all brackets are correctly nested and matched.
constraints: Length <= 100000; the empty string is valid.
questions.input_output: Call solve(input) with the JSON input shape in each fixture; return a JSON-compatible result.
hints: Keep the opening brackets that have not yet been closed.
questions.solution_code: function solve(value) { const stack=[],pairs={')':'(',']':'[','}':'{'}; for(const char of value){ if('([{'.includes(char)) stack.push(char); else if(stack.pop()!==pairs[char]) return false; } return stack.length===0; }
questions.detailed_explanation: Counting characters alone cannot validate nesting; the stack models unresolved structure. Keep the opening brackets that have not yet been closed.

questions.title: Next higher measurement
questions.question: Given integer measurements, return for each position the distance to the next strictly greater measurement, or 0 if none exists.
constraints: Length <= 100000; equal values are not greater.
questions.input_output: Call solve(input) with the JSON input shape in each fixture; return a JSON-compatible result.
hints: Retain unresolved indices in nonincreasing value order.
questions.solution_code: function solve(values) { const out=Array(values.length).fill(0),stack=[]; for(let i=0;i<values.length;i++){ while(stack.length && values[i]>values[stack[stack.length-1]]){const old=stack.pop();out[old]=i-old;} stack.push(i); } return out; }

questions.title: Find the first permitted position
questions.question: Input is {values,target} with ascending integers. Return the first index whose value is at least target, or values.length if no such index exists.

questions.solution_code: function solve({values,target}) { let low=0,high=values.length; while(low<high){const mid=low+Math.floor((high-low)/2);if(values[mid]<target) low=mid+1;else high=mid;} return low; }

questions.title: Stable merge ordering
questions.question: Given records {key,id}, return them sorted by ascending numeric key while preserving input order among equal keys. Implement merge sort rather than calling built-in sort.
constraints: At most 10000 records; ids are distinct strings.
questions.input_output: Call solve(input) with the JSON input shape in each fixture; return a JSON-compatible result.
hints: When keys tie, take from the left half first.

complexity.space: O(n) peak auxiliary plus O(log n) stack

questions.solution_code: function solve(items) { if(items.length<2)return items.slice(); const mid=Math.floor(items.length/2),a=solve(items.slice(0,mid)),b=solve(items.slice(mid)),out=[];let i=0,j=0;while(i<a.length&&j<b.length)out.push(a[i].key<=b[j].key?a[i++]:b[j++]);return out.concat(a.slice(i),b.slice(j)); }
questions.detailed_explanation: Insertion sorting can be quadratic; balanced merge recursion gives predictable comparison growth. When keys tie, take from the left half first.

State the invariant.
Time: O(n log n); auxiliary space: O(n) peak auxiliary plus O(log n) stack.

questions.title: Mutable range counter
questions.question: Input is {values,operations}. Operations are ['add',index,delta] or ['sum',left,right] with inclusive indices. Return each sum result. Use a Fenwick tree.
constraints: 1 <= values.length <= 10000; at most 10000 valid operations; sums remain safe integers.
questions.input_output: Call solve(input) with the JSON input shape in each fixture; return a JSON-compatible result.
hints: Convert external indices to one-based positions and define each low-bit range.

complexity.time: O((n + q) log n) with this simple construction

questions.solution_code: function solve({values,operations}) { const tree=Array(values.length+1).fill(0),out=[];function add(i,d){for(i++;i<tree.length;i+=i&-i)tree[i]+=d;}function prefix(i){let sum=0;for(i++;i>0;i-=i&-i)sum+=tree[i];return sum;}values.forEach((v,i)=>add(i,v));for(const [kind,a,b]of operations){if(kind==='add')add(a,b);else out.push(prefix(b)-prefix(a-1));}return out; }
questions.detailed_explanation: Plain prefixes make updates linear; Fenwick partial sums balance updates and queries logarithmically. Convert external indices to one-based positions and define each low-bit range.

questions.title: Idempotent batch boundary
questions.question: Given events {id,value}, return {accepted,duplicates}. Accept only the first occurrence of each id in input order; duplicates is the number of later occurrences. Do not mutate the input.
constraints: At most 10000 events; ids are strings; values are integers; deduplication applies only within this batch.
questions.input_output: Call solve(input) with the JSON input shape in each fixture; return a JSON-compatible result.
hints: Specify duplicate identity, scope and ordering before choosing the storage structure.
questions.solution_code: function solve(events) { const seen=new Set(),accepted=[];let duplicates=0;for(const event of events){if(seen.has(event.id)){duplicates++;continue;}seen.add(event.id);accepted.push({...event});}return {accepted,duplicates}; }
questions.detailed_explanation: This local function is not durable exactly-once delivery. Extend with transactional idempotency keys, validation and partial-failure tests in a separate API lab. Specify duplicate identity, scope and ordering before choosing the storage structure.

Time: O(n) expected; auxiliary space: O(n).

questions.title: Bounded asynchronous work
questions.question: Input is {values,limit}. Simulate asynchronous doubling using a resolved Promise for each item. Return doubled values in original input order, using no more than limit worker loops. Do not launch one Promise per input item up front.
constraints: 1 <= limit <= 10; at most 1000 values; this exercise models scheduling, not network or CPU parallelism.
questions.input_output: Call solve(input) with the JSON input shape in each fixture; return a JSON-compatible result.
hints: Claim an index before awaiting, and write its result back to that original index.
questions.solution_code: async function solve({values,limit}) { let next=0;const out=Array(values.length);async function worker(){while(next<values.length){const index=next++;out[index]=await Promise.resolve(values[index]*2);}}await Promise.all(Array.from({length:Math.min(limit,values.length)},()=>worker()));return out; }
questions.detailed_explanation: Output fixtures alone cannot prove the concurrency bound. Instrument active work in your own tests and discuss rejection, cancellation and thread-based races. Claim an index before awaiting, and write its result back to that original index.
expected_answer_elements: Claim an index before awaiting, and write its result back to that original index.
State the invariant.
Time: O(n) work; auxiliary space: O(limit) worker state excluding output.
